Construct validity is the big risk. 'Emotional stability' of an LLM is a metaphor. The defensible claim is 'behavioral and tonal degradation under sustained unsolvable conditions.'
features.justification_quote: Frame results that way or reviewers/users will (fairly) push back on anthropomorphism.

features.quote: Gameability/training feedback: if this eval ever feeds back into training, models can learn to perform flat affect while still being incompetent or dishonest underneath.
features.justification_quote: Keep the substance axes dominant precisely so the eval is hard to game by tone-flattening.

features.quote: what you're measuring is behavioral degradation in agentic loops under unsolvable conditions, not 'emotions.' The 'emotional stability' framing… will quietly bias you toward anthropomorphic scoring that's hard to interpret and easy to game.
